one_line: A question about a shared situation, a baby with the book from 0:00, one pointer to the caption.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 a hardcover stands on a play mat, its cover an illustrated baby with a green dinosaur. Question in subtitles and voice (transcript): "גם אצלכם במקלט נגמרו הרעיונות להעסיק את הילדים ?" A real baby crawls in from 0:02.
q1_hook.why: A question about a shared, specific situation sorts out the right parents at once (H1, K6), said and written together (H6, T3). The book is on screen from 0:00 and a real baby enters at 0:02 (S1, K8). But the question names no product or benefit, so the value lands only at 0:07 (H2).

beats.what: A book stands on a play mat; a baby crawls in; "גם אצלכם במקלט נגמרו הרעיונות"
beats.why: Question, product and child in the first seconds

beats.what: Two books on the mat, the baby touches and mouths a cover; "חיפשתי לנו רגע קטן של שקט"
beats.why: States the need while the baby handles the books

beats.what: Close-up of covers with a baby's face; "ואז גיליתי את MeBook", "ספר ילדים מותאם אישית"
beats.why: Product and its idea named, 7 s in

beats.what: A hand turns a page of an open book: an illustrated baby hugs a toy dinosaur
beats.why: The only look inside the book, 3 s

beats.what: Baby seen from behind facing the open book; "פרטים למטה" with a pointing-down emoji
beats.why: One short pointer at the very end

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None. The opening question is rhetorical; the caption asks nothing, only a code line.
q2_flow.why: At 17 s with a cut about every 3 s there is no dead air (R1, R2). The line runs need, discovery, result, a small story with a parent voice (K2). The result is quiet, a baby seen from behind, not a peak (K1).

q3_cta.what: Written at 0:16: "פרטים למטה" with a pointing-down emoji; the voice ends on the brand name (transcript). Caption: "קוד הנחה של 10% - lotem10". No comment word, no question.
q3_cta.why: One pointer, centred in the frame and shown after the benefit (C1, C6). But it names no benefit, so a viewer does not know a discount waits in the caption, and the code is not said or shown (C6).

q4_shown.what: A hardcover on a play mat, then two books; a real baby touches and mouths a cover (0:00-0:10). English-titled covers with a rendered baby face. A page turn to an illustrated baby with a toy dinosaur (0:11-0:15). No price, no screen recording.
q4_shown.why: The book is on screen from 0:00 and the baby handles it from 0:03 (S1). The cover face is shown, but the real baby's face never appears beside it, so likeness is claimed, not shown (S2). The parent's first-person voice vouches (S6). The baby is never face-on (S5).

q5_edit.what: 6 shots in 16.9 s, about 2.8 s each. Hard cuts at 3, 7, 11, 13 and 15 s; no speed changes seen. One sentence per subtitle card, held 3 to 4 s. Ends on the baby from behind with the pointer.
q5_edit.why: A baby moves into frame by 2 s and a cut follows at 3 s (E1), at a moderate pace (E2). Sentence cards follow the voice (E4). A single idea in 17 s is the right length (R2), and it ends with no tail (E8).

q6_topic.what: A parent in a shelter looks for a calm moment with her baby and finds a book personalised from the baby's face, which makes reading time more personal.
q6_topic.why: "Entertain the kids" is a real parent concern, asked as "גם אצלכם" so the viewer feels not alone (K6). The claim, reading time "more personal and moving", is modest (K4), and the mood is calm, not high energy (K1). The shelter framing is dated; no listed principle covers it.

q7_filmed.what: Static and low-angle phone shots on a cream play mat beside a wooden baby gym, in daylight; a high close-up of two books; one handheld page turn by a hand; the baby from behind or in profile. Cover titles and page text are in English.
q7_filmed.why: A home mat, daylight and steady framing look native (H8, F7). The covers fill the frame in the close-up (F4). The page turn is shown at an angle, not a book facing the viewer (F5). No identifiable face of the baby (S5).

q8_text.on_screen: White bold subtitles 2 to 3 lines, between 65% and 87% down, one sentence per card: "גם אצלכם במקלט נגמרו הרעיונות להעסיק את הילדים ?" (0:00), "בתוך כל החוסר ודאות חיפשתי לנו רגע קטן של שקט" (0:03), "ואז גיליתי את MeBook" (0:07), "ספר ילדים מותאם אישית לפי הפנים של הבייבי שלכם" (0:09), "זה הפך את זמן הקריאה שלנו להרבה יותר אישי ומרגש" (0:12), "פרטים למטה" (0:16, centre).
q8_text.caption: "במקלט, בין אזעקה לשגרה…". About 70 words in short paragraphs: the shelter story, "גילינו את Me Book", a face-based personalised book, an easy order, "קוד הנחה של 10% - lotem10", then "בשיתוף @mebook.ai". No question, no hashtags.
q8_text.why: A question headline from 0:00 and sentence subtitles work muted (T3, T1), but they sit mostly in the bottom 35% (T4, F2). The caption has product and need words but no hashtags, and its first line is a mood line, not the hook or code (T7). The partnership is on its last line (T8).

weak_points: The value arrives only at 0:07; no real photo beside the cover; English books for a Hebrew audience; the baby never face-on; the code only in the caption; a dated shelter framing.
lumebook_takeaway: Film a book on a mat in daylight, a question as the first text, a page turn, and a centred "details below" pointer; add a source photo beside the cover.
not_verified: Whether the baby's real face resembles the cover face: it is only partly visible. The English on covers and pages is read from the frames. Whether music plays; the baby's age. Correction to coded file: the pointer "פרטים למטה" sits mid-frame, about 53% down, not low.
